name: Learjet 23/24/25
summary: The original Learjets, small and fast turbojet-powered business jets from the 1960s-70s that are still flown by cargo, charter and test operators.

wings: Low swept wing with large tip tanks on most
engines: Two small GE CJ610 turbojets in slim pods on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Very slim, small fuselage with a few small windows

tellTales: Slim tip tanks on a small swept-wing jet with a T-tail
Very slim fuselage with a short row of tiny windows
Small, slender rear engine pods (turbojets, not fans)

confusedWith.howToTell: The 35 has fatter turbofan pods and a longer fuselage; the 23/24/25 has slimmer turbojet pods and a smaller fuselage.
The 55/60 has small winglets and a much larger cabin; the 23/24/25 has tip tanks and a tiny fuselage.
The Westwind has a low-set tailplane and a bigger, rounder body; the Lear has a T-tail and a slimmer body.
The Falcon 10 has no tip tanks and a larger, rounder cabin; the Lear has tip tanks and a pencil-slim fuselage.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
